narrative.text: Oberlin enters your study carrying a heavy iron lockbox. She sets it on your desk with a thud. 'We raided a hidden BNI safehouse in the old quarter,' she says. 'This was buried under the floorboards.'

Inside are the Blackmail Files. The BNI spent 20 years compiling dossiers on every major politician in Veltria. Sexual affairs, financial crimes, secret memberships. Half the Assembly is in here. The BNI was using these files to keep the politicians in line under Halvek.

My God. This is the ultimate leverage. With these files, you can guarantee the passage of any legislation you want. You can destroy Kolvar's entire coalition. Or you can burn them and prove you are better than Halvek.

I hold the sins of the entire Assembly in an iron box. With a word, I can own every vote in the chamber. I can pass the budget, the reforms, the constitution—everything—without a single fight. But that is exactly what Halvek did. He used the BNI to control the state. If I use these files, I become him. If I burn them, those corrupt politicians walk free, and I fight every battle uphill.

choices.text: Use the files. Blackmail the Assembly into passing your agenda.
Burn the files publicly. Expose the corrupt politicians and let the chips fall.
Lock them in Krel's vault. 'Just in case.'

narrative.text: I open the box and read twelve files before I stop. That is enough. The first vote I need comes from a man whose 1951 financial records I now hold. I send a message through Vyktor — nothing explicit, just a meeting request and a reference to a date. He votes correctly the following week. The second goes the same way. By the third, I no longer need to send messages. The word has traveled through its own channels. I have the votes I need. I also have something else now — an awareness that I cannot put back in the box.

choices.text: Three votes from twelve files. The rest of the box is still open.

narrative.text: We burned them in the courtyard. Oberlin, Vyktor, and I. It took forty minutes. Some of the files were thick. Vyktor watched without speaking — I could see him calculating what we had just destroyed. Three assembly members who had been on Krel's watch list will never know how close they came to having their histories used against them. Kolvar is one of them. I burned his file without reading it. I want that on the record, at least internally: I burned it without reading it.
The morning gardener sweeps the ash from the courtyard. He asks no questions and is given a day's extra pay, which he didn't ask for either.

choices.text: Forty minutes of fire in the courtyard. Kolvar's file burned unread.

narrative.text: Krel takes the box without comment. It goes into the secure archive beneath the Ministry of Interior, catalogued under a reference number that means nothing to anyone without the index. I have not used it. I have not burned it. I have made the decision that the decision can wait, which is its own kind of decision. Vyktor said nothing when I told him. He looked at the space where the box had been and then looked at me. I told him it was temporary. He nodded the way he nods when he does not believe something but has decided not to argue it today.

choices.text: The box sits in the Interior vault under a number nobody knows. Undecided is also a decision.
